title: Mixed to 20
subtitle: + − to 20, × ÷ to 10
bounds: Mixed facts (PROTOCOL 4c, briefs/facts2): the whole run inside + and − to 20 and × and ÷ with factors to 10, easy to hard by tier. Each tier is 6 items from each of facts-add-20, facts-sub-20, facts-mul-10, facts-div-10 at the same tier: the same pools, forms, distractors, explanations and student text, every part's floor n scaled to ceil(n / 4), at most 2 zero-factor multiplication prompts a tier; 24 items per tier, prompts unique per tier, operations interleaved. Misconception keys carry their operation (ADD_, SUB_, MUL_, DIV_). Answer rank among the 4 values 15-35% each over the whole tier. [ADD] Facts bounds (PROTOCOL 4c, briefs/facts2): the whole run inside sums 11 to 20, easy to hard by tier. Prompt forms: R 'a + b = ?' (answer s), C 'a + ? = s' (answer b), S '? + b = s' (answer a); every number a non-negative integer. T1 R, a ten-plus number and no new ten (12 + 5). T2 R, a, b >= 2: doubles, neighbours (7 + 8) and the nines (9 + 6, one digit each). T3 R, both one digit. T4 C, a, b >= 2 (>= 12 with both one digit). T5 S (>= 12, >= 6 with both one digit) and C with both one digit. Prompts unique per tier, 24 per tier. Wrong choices: distinct non-negative integers <= 999, >= 2 near the answer (+-1, +-2, +-10), at most 1 far; answer rank among the 4 values 15-35% each per tier; answers >= 20 always have a wrong choice sharing the ones digit (+-10); the answer is never the only value of its parity. [SUB] Minuends 11-20, a and b at least 1. T1 R with one of s, a, b at least 10 and no trade (13 − 3, 17 − 4); T2 R doubles, near doubles and nines (a, b at least 2); T3 R, a and b both one digit; T4 s − ? = b, a and b 2 or more, at least 12 with both one digit; T5 ? − a = b, a and b 2 or more (at least 12; at least 6 with both one digit) plus s − ? = b one digit. Wrong choices: distinct non-negative integers up to 999, at least two within 1, 2 or 10 of the answer, at most one far; where the answer is 20 or more one wrong choice shares its ones digit; modelled misconceptions first, ARITH only to fill; each answer rank (smallest to largest of the four) holds the answer in 15-35% of a tier. [MUL] Factors 0 to 10. Forms: R a × b = ?, C a × ? = p, S ? × b = p (a missing factor is never 0). T1 R: a fact with 0, 1, 2, 5 or 10 (85 prompts); T2 R: facts from 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9 with a 3, 4 or 9 (27; at least 8 with both factors in 3, 4, 9); T3 R: a 6, 7 or 8 (27; at least 8 with both in 6, 7, 8); T4 C: at least 12 from 3, 4, 6-9 on both factors, else any factors 2-10 (81 prompts); T5 S: at least 12 from 3, 4, 6-9 on both factors, plus C from the same (72). At most 6 prompts per tier with a 0 factor. Wrong choices are distinct non-negative whole numbers up to 999. R: at least two within the larger factor of the answer (at least 2), at most one far. C and S: at least two within 2 of the answer, at most one far. Answer ranks (smallest to largest of the four) each hold 15 to 35 percent of a tier. [DIV] PROTOCOL 4c, facts range cartridge. Forms: R is p ÷ a = ? (answer the quotient), C is p ÷ ? = b (answer the divisor), S is ? ÷ a = b (answer the dividend); p = a × b, the times table read backwards, never ÷ 0, no 0 ÷ ? = 0. Divisors and quotients 0-10. T1 R: a or b in {0,1,2,5,10}. T2 R: facts of 3, 4, 9 (a, b both in {3,4,9} at least 8). T3 R: facts of 6, 7, 8 (a, b both in {6,7,8} at least 8). T4 C: a, b in {3,4,6,7,8,9} (at least 12) plus C with a, b 2-10. T5 S: a, b in {3,4,6,7,8,9} (at least 12) plus C on the same pairs. Wrong choices: distinct non-negative integers up to 999, at least 2 near and at most 1 far. R: near within 2 of the quotient (GROUP_OFF q+-1, +-2), far SUBTRACTED p-a, MULTIPLIED p×a, TENS_SLIP q+-10. C: near within 2 of the divisor (MISSING_ONE_OFF a+-1, ARITH +-2), far MISSING_SUBTRACTED p-b, MISSING_MULTIPLIED p×b. S: near within the larger factor of the dividend (START_GROUP_OFF p+-a, START_ADDED a+b, START_TENS p+-10 when a factor is 11 or more, with a twin ones digit when p is 20 or more). The answer's rank among the four values is spread 15-35% per tier.

ADD_ONE_OFF.student: Off by one. Count again: start at the bigger number and count up.
ADD_ONE_OFF.teacher: Counted on wrong: the sum is one more or one less than the true sum.

ADD_SUBTRACTED.student: Plus means put together. Add the two numbers, don't take them apart.
ADD_SUBTRACTED.teacher: Subtracted the smaller addend from the larger instead of adding: 8 + 5 = 3.

ADD_NO_CARRY.student: The ones made a new ten. Add that ten in with the tens.
ADD_NO_CARRY.teacher: Dropped the regrouped ten when the ones summed to 10 or more: 38 + 47 = 75.

ADD_TENS_SLIP.student: Check the tens place. Add the tens, then the ones.
ADD_TENS_SLIP.teacher: Tens digit of the sum is one too many or too few, with the ones right: 34 + 52 = 76 or 96.

ADD_MISSING_ADDED.student: Don't add the two numbers you see. Find the missing one: subtract.
ADD_MISSING_ADDED.teacher: Added the shown number and the total instead of subtracting: 7 + ? = 15 answered 22.

ADD_MISSING_ONE_OFF.student: Off by one. Add your answer to the shown number and check the total.
ADD_MISSING_ONE_OFF.teacher: Counted up wrong: the missing number is one more or one less than the true one.

ADD_MISSING_TENS.student: Check the tens. Add your answer to the shown number: is it the total?
ADD_MISSING_TENS.teacher: Missing number is ten too many or too few: forgot the trade counting up across a ten, or a tens slip.

SUB_ONE_OFF.student: Off by one. Check: answer + number taken away must equal the start.
SUB_ONE_OFF.teacher: Counted back one step too many or too few: answer is the correct difference plus or minus 1.

SUB_ADDED.student: Take away, don't add. Subtracting makes the number smaller.
SUB_ADDED.teacher: Added the two numbers (s + a) instead of subtracting.

SUB_SMALLER_FROM_LARGER.student: Don't flip digits. If the top digit is smaller, trade a ten for 10 ones.
SUB_SMALLER_FROM_LARGER.teacher: In each place takes the smaller digit from the larger (14 - 6 gives 12; 52 - 38 gives 26) instead of regrouping.

SUB_FORGOT_TRADE.student: You traded a ten for ones, so the tens digit has to drop by one.
SUB_FORGOT_TRADE.teacher: Regrouped the ones but left the tens unchanged: answer is 10 too big (14 - 6 gives 18; 52 - 38 gives 24).

SUB_TENS_SLIP.student: The tens are off by one ten. Check: answer + taken away = start.
SUB_TENS_SLIP.teacher: Right ones, tens digit one too high or too low: answer is the correct difference plus or minus 10.

SUB_MISSING_ADDED.student: Add the missing part to what is left and you must get the start. Check it.
SUB_MISSING_ADDED.teacher: s - ? = b: added the two numbers shown (s + b) instead of finding what was taken away.

SUB_MISSING_ONE_OFF.student: Off by one. Put your number back in the problem and check it.
SUB_MISSING_ONE_OFF.teacher: Missing number is one too big or too small (the answer plus or minus 1); did not check by substituting.

SUB_MISSING_TENS.student: Off by one ten. Put your number back in the problem and check it.
SUB_MISSING_TENS.teacher: Right ones, tens digit one too high or too low: the missing number plus or minus 10 (trade forgotten or tens slip).

SUB_START_SUBTRACTED.student: The start is bigger than both numbers: add back what was taken away.
SUB_START_SUBTRACTED.teacher: ? - a = b: took the two shown numbers apart (|b - a|) instead of adding back what was taken.

MUL_GROUP_OFF.student: One group too many or too few. Count the groups, then the size of each.
MUL_GROUP_OFF.teacher: Off by one group: a × (b + 1), a × (b − 1), (a + 1) × b or (a − 1) × b.

MUL_ADDED.student: × means equal groups, not +. 4 × 3 is 4 groups of 3, which is 12.
MUL_ADDED.teacher: Adds the factors instead of multiplying: 4 × 3 = 7.

MUL_MISSING_ONE_OFF.student: Check it: multiply your number by the shown one. Does it make the total?
MUL_MISSING_ONE_OFF.teacher: Missing factor one too high or too low: counted the groups wrong, or never multiplied back to check.

MUL_MISSING_SUBTRACTED.student: Not subtraction. Ask: this number times what makes the total?
MUL_MISSING_SUBTRACTED.teacher: Subtracts the shown factor from the product (p − k) instead of dividing the product by it.

MUL_MISSING_PRODUCT.student: The total is the product, not the missing factor. Multiply back to check.
MUL_MISSING_PRODUCT.teacher: Writes the product as the missing factor: the number already given in the equation.

DIV_GROUP_OFF.student: Close: a group or two off. Multiply your answer by the divisor to check.
DIV_GROUP_OFF.teacher: Quotient off by one or two: counted a group or two too many or too few.

DIV_SUBTRACTED.student: Divide, don't subtract. Ask how many of the divisor fit in the dividend.
DIV_SUBTRACTED.teacher: Subtracts the divisor from the dividend (p − a) instead of dividing.

DIV_MULTIPLIED.student: Divide, don't multiply. Ask how many of the divisor fit in the dividend.
DIV_MULTIPLIED.teacher: Multiplies dividend and divisor (p × a) instead of dividing.

DIV_MISSING_ONE_OFF.student: One off. Try your number in the problem: does the division work out?
DIV_MISSING_ONE_OFF.teacher: Missing divisor off by one: stopped a fact early or late in the table.

DIV_MISSING_SUBTRACTED.student: Don't subtract. Ask: what times the answer shown makes the dividend?
DIV_MISSING_SUBTRACTED.teacher: Subtracts (p − b) to find the missing divisor instead of asking what times b makes p.

DIV_MISSING_MULTIPLIED.student: Too big. Divide the dividend by your number: is it the answer shown?
DIV_MISSING_MULTIPLIED.teacher: Multiplies (p × b) to find the missing divisor instead of dividing or asking what times b makes p.

DIV_START_GROUP_OFF.student: One group off. Multiply the two numbers you see, no more, no less.
DIV_START_GROUP_OFF.teacher: Missing dividend off by one divisor (a × (b +- 1)): counted one group too many or too few.

DIV_START_ADDED.student: Don't add. To undo dividing, multiply the two numbers you see.
DIV_START_ADDED.teacher: Adds the divisor and quotient (a + b) to find the missing dividend instead of multiplying back.

items.explanation: 5 × 8 = 40: half of 8 × 10 = 80, and half of 80 is 40.
10 × 10 = 100: ten groups of 10, so put a zero after 10.
9 × 10 = 90: ten groups of 9, so put a zero after 9.
6 × 5 = 30: half of 6 × 10 = 60, and half of 60 is 30.
3 + 13 = 16: ones first, 3 + 3 = 6, and the ten makes 16.
11 + 5 = 16: ones first, 1 + 5 = 6, and the ten makes 16.
12 + 4 = 16: ones first, 2 + 4 = 6, and the ten makes 16.
11 + 8 = 19: ones first, 1 + 8 = 9, and the ten makes 19.
0 ÷ 5 = 0: zero shared into groups of 5 leaves none, and 5 × 0 = 0.
6 × 10 = 60: ten groups of 6, so put a zero after 6.
18 ÷ 3 = 6 because 3 × 6 = 18. Neighbour fact: 3 × 5 = 15, plus one more 3.
13 − 4: take 3 to get 10, then take 1 more: 9. Check: 4 + 9 = 13.
6 + 9 = 15: 6 + 10 = 16, and 9 is one less than 10, so 15.
14 − 9: take 4 to get 10, then take 5 more: 5. Check: 9 + 5 = 14.
9 + 7 = 16: 7 + 10 = 17, and 9 is one less than 10, so 16.
7 + 9 = 16: 7 + 10 = 17, and 9 is one less than 10, so 16.
12 ÷ 3 = 4 because 3 × 4 = 12. Neighbour fact: 3 × 3 = 9, plus one more 3.
7 + 7 = 14: a double. Doubles are worth knowing by heart.
13 − 6: take 3 to get 10, then take 3 more: 7. Check: 6 + 7 = 13.
15 − 8: take 5 to get 10, then take 3 more: 7. Check: 8 + 7 = 15.
9 ÷ 3 = 3 because 3 × 3 = 9. Neighbour fact: 3 × 2 = 6, plus one more 3.
14 − 5: take 4 to get 10, then take 1 more: 9. Check: 5 + 9 = 14.
15 − 7: take 5 to get 10, then take 2 more: 8. Check: 7 + 8 = 15.
48 ÷ 8 = 6 because 8 × 6 = 48. Neighbour fact: 8 × 5 = 40, plus one more 8.
13 − 8: take 3 to get 10, then take 5 more: 5. Check: 8 + 5 = 13.
7 + 7 = 14: a double. Doubles are worth knowing by heart.
12 − 9: take 2 to get 10, then take 7 more: 3. Check: 9 + 3 = 12.
7 + 9 = 16: 7 + 10 = 17, and 9 is one less than 10, so 16.
24 ÷ 4 = 6 because 4 × 6 = 24. Neighbour fact: 4 × 5 = 20, plus one more 4.
56 ÷ 8 = 7 because 8 × 7 = 56. Neighbour fact: 8 × 6 = 48, plus one more 8.
12 − 8: take 2 to get 10, then take 6 more: 4. Check: 8 + 4 = 12.
24 ÷ 3 = 8 because 3 × 8 = 24. Neighbour fact: 3 × 7 = 21, plus one more 3.
14 − 8: take 4 to get 10, then take 4 more: 6. Check: 8 + 6 = 14.
12 − 4: take 2 to get 10, then take 2 more: 8. Check: 4 + 8 = 12.
21 ÷ 3 = 7 because 3 × 7 = 21. Neighbour fact: 3 × 6 = 18, plus one more 3.
19 − ? = 12: count up from 12 to 19, that is 7. So 19 − 7 = 12, ? = 7.
11 − ? = 2: count up from 2 to 11, that is 9. So 11 − 9 = 2, ? = 9.
4 × ? = 12: 4 × 3 = 12, so ? = 3. Count by 4s up to 12, or divide: 12 ÷ 4 = 3.
6 × ? = 48: 6 × 8 = 48, so ? = 8. Count by 6s up to 48, or divide: 48 ÷ 6 = 8.
7 × ? = 56: 7 × 8 = 56, so ? = 8. Count by 7s up to 56, or divide: 56 ÷ 7 = 8.
11 − ? = 3: count up from 3 to 11, that is 8. So 11 − 8 = 3, ? = 8.
10 + ? = 20: 10 + 10 = 20, so ? = 10. Count up by tens: add 1 ten to 10.
8 × ? = 80: 8 × 10 = 80, so ? = 10. Count by 8s up to 80, or divide: 80 ÷ 8 = 10.
16 − ? = 9: count up from 9 to 16, that is 7. So 16 − 7 = 9, ? = 7.
4 × ? = 28: 4 × 7 = 28, so ? = 7. Count by 4s up to 28, or divide: 28 ÷ 4 = 7.
17 − ? = 6: count up from 6 to 17, that is 11. So 17 − 11 = 6, ? = 11.
14 − ? = 7: count up from 7 to 14, that is 7. So 14 − 7 = 7, ? = 7.
? × 6 = 48: 8 × 6 = 48, so ? = 8. Count by 6s up to 48, or divide: 48 ÷ 6 = 8.
16 ÷ ? = 4: 4 × 4 = 16, so ? = 4. A square fact: 4 times itself makes 16.
? × 4 = 28: 7 × 4 = 28, so ? = 7. Count by 4s up to 28, or divide: 28 ÷ 4 = 7.
8 × ? = 56: 8 × 7 = 56, so ? = 7. Count by 8s up to 56, or divide: 56 ÷ 8 = 7.
? × 9 = 36: 4 × 9 = 36, so ? = 4. Count by 9s up to 36, or divide: 36 ÷ 9 = 4.
? − 8 = 4: undo the take away, 4 + 8 = 12, so ? = 12. Check: 12 − 8 = 4.
6 × ? = 36: 6 × 6 = 36, so ? = 6. Count by 6s up to 36, or divide: 36 ÷ 6 = 6.
? × 3 = 9: 3 × 3 = 9, so ? = 3. Count by 3s up to 9, or divide: 9 ÷ 3 = 3.
